title: Qin Dynasty
capsule: The Qin dynasty was the first unified imperial polity of China, founded when King Zheng of Qin completed the conquest of the six Warring States rivals between 230 and 221 BCE and proclaimed himself Qin Shi Huang, the First Emperor. His government standardized weights, measures, script, and axle-widths across a realm of roughly three million square kilometers, and constructed the earliest linked defensive walls later elaborated into the Great Wall. The dynasty was cripplingly brief: Qin Shi Huang died in 210 BCE, and a succession crisis combined with mass peasant revolt led by Chen Sheng and later Liu Bang brought the regime down by 206 BCE, paving the way for the Han dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Qin realm's extent is well documented in Han-era sources and confirmed by archaeological finds including the First Emperor's mausoleum; provincial boundaries within the empire are subject to ongoing revision.
